reviews.comment: While I struggle at times to understand the material in the course, Prof. Srinivasa truly cares about the students in his class and how they learn. He wants everything handwritten and allowed us to use notes on exams and quizzes. He responds to discussion questions and holds office hours regularly. He has a great teaching style!
reviews.ratingTags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Explains unnecessary things for too long (took 2 weeks to get into class material), and barely explains complicated topics. Unorganized and did not teach the material well at all. Tests were different from homework and contained materials that were not covered. Try to avoid for 305.

He does not follow slides, does not show his work, and his notes are nearly impossible to follow. Exams were open note open books, but that doesn't really matter when the material was barely covered, if at all, and the book is not helpful

Very unorganized lectures, that are very hard to follow. The final review was uploaded 5 days before the exam at 9pm at night, when we're all studying for other exams during finals. The final review was a 68-page document and very unorganized and hard to read. It was useless. The first exam review was readable and well organized, very good on that.

Unfortunately, this is Dr. S's first sem of teaching 305, and his lectures/notes/slides were all very disorganized and helped very little with what the homework and tests covered. His handwriting can be sloppy, and his lectures are not clear with regard to solving problems and using necessary equations. He may get better as he does more 305 though.
reviews.ratingTags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Goes into random tangents all the time and has terrible terrible notes, none of which make any sense outside of class. He talk super quiet and has a thick accent which makes his lectures super difficult to follow, and consistently went over the time limit with quizzes or work assignments every single class.
Unplanned lectures. Poor pacing. Homework is due the same day you complete the material. No canvas organization.

His class was always fun and interesting. He knew the course was hard so he always tried to give us help, feedback, or make it easier if too many people struggled. Hw is on the harder side because he makes it ambiguous on purpose. Really caring and great prof. Tests aren't too bad as we're given spreadsheets to use

Dr. Srinivasa really cares that you learn Solids. He makes the lengthy calculations very manageable with the excel sheets. So long as you know how to approach a problem, this class will not be bad. Especially since this is known to be one of the most rough courses, Srinivasa is the way to go!

One of the big 3 in MEEN (364, 368, 461). Does a really nice job conveying the material without making the class difficult. He gives you all the hints to get an A in his class, so listen to his advice. Easy B, midterm and final determine the A. Overall, best choice for this course and no blindsiding on the exams.

The absolute best for Solids. First third is drive trains, second is shafts, and last is frames. It is essentially 360 and 305/489 on steroids. He has conceptual quiz a week, weekly hw's starting week 5, 4-phase semester project, midterm (20%), final (20%). He gives you pointers on how to ace his class and gives you all the tools needed to succeed.

He knows what he is talking about. It can be a bit frustrating when he sends project requirements 24 hours before the deadline. 225 Honors is definitely more difficult than the regular section. Therefore, the exams are more difficult. Expect to see questions that you have not seen before. Take that as a precursor to your engineering career.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: While Srinivasa is a great professor, the one complaint I have is he is almost never available outside of class.  Most of that is he's one of the Assistant Heads of Mechanical Engineering so he has an excuse to be busy.  But unless you never have to ask questions or discuss grades, I would avoid his classes.

By far and away the best professor in the MEEN department. You don't necessarily need to go to class but he is an extremely good teacher. Highly recommend him for 225 because he teaches it the way that it is used later on in upper level classes.  Able to relate what you learn to actual real world engineering examples.

Lectures are "optional" in the sense that you don't have to go if you don't want to. But he does little online quizzes based on the homework and videos at the beginning of most classes. He basically motivational speaks while he teaches. He makes you really excited for mechanical engineering. He teaches and answers questions well. Entertaining too.

Hands down the best professor I've had here so far. Lectures are interesting and very helpful. Has a good sense of humor. Genuinely cares about students learning. Mandatory homework every week and supplemental online lectures - taking the time to understand them is key to doing well on tests. Would definitely take a class with this professor again.

Dr. Arun Srinivasa is one of the best professors to have taught mechanical engineering at the TAMU-Q campus, simply because he was a breath of fresh air. Great at giving real world examples and seems enthusiastic about teaching the course.
Thinks he is funny, sometimes is. Explains himself again if he thinks he can explain the point differently. Takes a practical approach to teaching.
Great teacher, walks you through the material so you understand it. Wants to help those who want to succeed. Highly reccommend taking his class
"The math yall learn here in america could go up my nose and not even make me sneeze"   "Is that obvious to you?"
No Comments

He was kinda hard to understand sometimes because of his accent, but he taught the material very well. He would also repeat himself if he knew he had said something too fast. I would take one of his classes again.
